slides.title: Developmental MilestonesErikson
text: Infant- birth to 1 year- Trust vs Mistrust
Toddler- 1-3 years- Autonomy vs Shame & Doubt
Adolescent- 12-20 years- Identity vs Role Confusion
Young Adult- 20-35 years- Intimacy vs Isolation
Middle Adult- 35-65 years- Generativity vs Stagnation
Older Adult- 65 and older- Integrity vs Despair

slides.title: Interaction with Children
text: INFANT: If asleep, auscultate the heart, lungs and abdomen first, traumatic procedures last
TODDLERS AND PRESCHOOLERS: No head to toe, may need to sit on caregiver's lap
SCHOOL AGE: Still concrete thinkers, be careful of language used,  like to play with equipment
ADOLESCENTS: Give them respect and privacy, be honest and involve them

slides.title: Infant and Toddler Vital Sign Measurement
text: Infant and Toddler Vital Sign Measurement
Count respirations FIRST (before disturbing the child)

slides.title: Pediatric Pain Management
text: Questioning the child based on developmental level
FACES pain rating scale can be used 3 and under
Visual analog and numerical scales ages 7 and older

slides.title: Pediatric Pain Management
text: Relaxation – holding, stroking, soft voice, etc. (counting, music, games)

slides.title: Acute Infectious Diseases
text: Sudden onset at hour of sleep

slides.title: Acute Infectious Diseases
text: Caused by  H.influenzae type B (Hib vaccine prevents this)
Sudden high fever, drooling, restlessness, anxiety, tripod position

slides.title: Acute Infectious Diseases
text: Inflammation of the tonsils (may be caused by Strep)
If chronic have tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy
Popsicles, ice, encourage fluids, no citrus – red, brown fluids

slides.title: Otitis Media
text: Infection (bacterial/viral) of fluid in middle ear
Fever, otalgia (ear pain), irritable, crying, inconsolably, pulling at ears
Acetaminophen/ibuprofen for mild to moderate pain

slides.title: Cystic fibrosis
text: Loss of sodium and chloride in sweat
Salty taste to skin, steatorrhea, delayed growth, poor wt. gain, chronic resp. dysfunction, wheezing, nail clubbing

slides.title: Chronic Diseases
text: Positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP) or CPAP
Administer fat soluble vitamins (A,D, E, K)

slides.title: Pediatric Cardiology
text: With 1st breath= pressure changes result in closure of openings in the heart
Point of maximal impact( PMI) is located at the fourth intercostal space just medial of the child's left midclavicular line until age 4
Left midclavicular line at the fifth intercostal space in children ages 7 and over

slides.title: Congenital Heart Disease
text: Disorders with decreased pulmonary blood flow  (Cyanotic)
Disorders with increased pulmonary blood flow (Acyanotic)

slides.title: Congenital Heart Disease
text: Opening between the aorta and pulmonary artery
Usually closes within 72 hours after birth

slides.title: Congenital Heart Disease
text: Obstruction below, at, or after the aortic valve

slides.title: Congenital Heart Disease
text: Pulmonary artery and aorta do not separate

slides.title: Congenital Heart Disease
text: Assisting the child and family to cope
Preventing infection – RSV prophylaxis, hand hygiene, dental care

slides.title: Cardiovascular Disorders
text: Injures the heart, blood vessels, and valves
Fever, large joint pain, chorea, erythema marginatum (rash), murmur, subcutaneous nodules
Antibiotics, corticosteroids, NSAIDs, haloperidol (Haldol) for chorea
Prophylactic antibiotics prior to dental visit

slides.title: Cardiovascular Disorders

Occurs mainly in Japanese or  Korean children under age 5
High fever for more than 5 days ( unresponsive to antibiotics)

don't allow rubbing of sutures, clean suture line as ordered, “logan bow” or butterfly adhesive to protect suture line, prevent vigorous crying
Promoting adequate nutrition: use of special devices, burp frequency, hold upright
Encouraging infant–parent bonding: encourage holding, acknowledge feelings, support/education

slides.title: Skeletal Disorders
text: Changes cause pain, redness, warmth, stiffness, swelling, fever, rash

slides.title: Skeletal Disorders
text: Abnormal development of the femoral head
Wear Pavlik harness if under 6 months
Surgical correction if over 6 months (Spica Cast)

slides.title: Neuromuscular Disorders
text: Defect of the vertebral bodies without protrusion of the spinal cord or meninges
Meninges herniate through defect in vertebrae
Spinal cord usually normal, typically no associated neuro deficits
If skin/sac intact; surgery may be delayed

slides.title: Neuromuscular Disorders
text: Neural tube fails to close end of 4th week
External sac contains meninges, spinal fluid, nerves
Lack of prenatal folic acid or anticonvulsant use

slides.title: Neuromuscular Disorders
text: Corticosteroids slow progression, calcium supplements, braces

slides.title: Neuromuscular Disorders
text: Non-progressive damage to the motor areas of the brain
Causes include maternal infections, kernicterus, anoxia associated with birth
Child must be fed upright and support lower jaw

slides.title: Hydrocephalus
text: Abnormal accumulation of CSF in the ventricles of the brain

slides.title: Neurological Infectious Disorders
text: Usually caused by strep or N. Meningitidis
Administer antibiotics, isolate 24 hours, keep area dark and quiet, seizure precautions

slides.title: Neurological Infectious Disorders
text: Acute rapidly progressing encephalopathy and fatty liver development
Associated with viral infections and   aspirin use

slides.title: Chromosomal Abnormalities
text: Flat broad nose, protruding tongue, upward slanted eye folds, palmar crease (simian)
Feed to back and side of mouth

slides.title: Trauma
text: Violet shaking of an infant resulting in intracranial trauma
Monitor for signs of increased ICP

slides.title: Child Abuse
text: Neglect, physical, sexual, and emotional maltreatment

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Question
text: The nurse in the pediatric clinic is caring for a 6-year-old client with recurrent group A streptococcal pharyngitis and inflammation of the conjunctivae. The eyelids are edematous. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
Moisten a clean compress with warm water.
Remind the client to avoid rubbing their eyes.
Instill newly prescribed antibiotic drops in both eyes.
Wipe each client eye beginning at the inner canthus.
